title: tenant_default shadow table (from unqualified CREATE TABLE tenant in 031_adp04b_tenant_realm_binding.sql) causes schema drift; OutOfOrderMigration false-positive on cold-start db_test
affected_areas: any unqualified INSERT/UPDATE/SELECT against `tenant` issued while search_path includes a tenant schema before public
notes:
Discovered while implementing ISS-0100 (GitHub #357) Iteration 1 (GBL-086/102 guard scoping + helpers.zig SVC fixture hygiene). Two distinct, compounding pre-existing defects, both reproducible on main with zero ISS-0100 changes present (confirmed via baseline stash-and-compare):

(1) Shadow tenant_default.tenant table: migration 031_adp04b_tenant_realm_binding.sql contains an UNQUALIFIED `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tenant (...)`. Because this file is not GBL-prefixed, src/db/migrations.zig's per-schema skip logic (lines 196-207, GBL-prefix-only) does not exclude it from non-public schemas, so it creates a duplicate `tenant` table inside tenant_default (and presumably any other provisioned tenant schema). Later GBL-prefixed migrations that add columns to public.tenant (e.g. GBL-080's tenant_type) are, by design, never applied to this shadow copy. tests/integration/helpers.zig::configureTestSearchPath sets `search_path TO tenant_default,public` on every TestHarness.init(), so any unqualified `INSERT INTO tenant (...)` issued afterward (e.g. the SVC-01..04 fixture block in ensureDefaultOidcSeeds, prior to the ISS-0100 fix) silently resolves against the stale shadow table and fails once a GBL-only column is referenced (`column "tenant_type" of relation "tenant" does not exist`). Verified reproducible on both a long-lived warmed-up db_test and a freshly recreated one. Fixed locally within ISS-0100's own two files by schema-qualifying every `tenant` reference in ensureDefaultOidcSeeds as `public.tenant` -- but every OTHER unqualified reference to `tenant` anywhere in the codebase (other test helpers, migrations, application code) remains equally exposed.

(2) OutOfOrderMigration false positive on true cold-start: recreating db_test from a completely empty Docker volume and immediately running the full integration suite (zig build test-integration-svc, which aggregates all ~543 integration tests via tests/integration/main_test.zig) reproducibly fails the very first TestHarness.init() call with error.OutOfOrderMigration from src/db/migrations.zig. Confirmed via baseline (no ISS-0100 changes) comparison: identical failure on main. Does NOT reproduce when db_test is first fully migrated via the standalone `migrate` binary (BPM_DB_URL repointed at the test port) -- all 95 migrations apply cleanly for both public and tenant_default schemas that way -- then the test suite is run against that already-migrated state. Root cause not fully isolated; duplicate numeric migration-file prefixes exist on disk (050_tenant_hostnames.sql / 050_xc01_trace_id_audit.sql, and 056_onboarding_registry.sql / 056_xc03_configuration_repository_fix.sql) and are a candidate contributing factor, though not proven as the direct trigger under the strict-less-than out-of-order guard.

Neither defect blocks normal pipeline operation because db_test is a long-lived container that already has all migrations applied in practice; both are latent risks for any future environment reset, CI cold-start, or new-developer onboarding. Full evidence trail: baseline run (before ISS-0100 changes, warm db_test) = 462 pass / 7 skip / 74 fail (543 total); with only the mechanical helpers.zig SVC tenant_type addition and no schema-qualification fix = 132 pass / 404 fail (regression, cascading from (1)); with the schema-qualification fix added = 474 pass / 7 skip / 62 fail (543 total) -- an improvement over baseline, with all 62 remaining failures independently confirmed unrelated to tenant/tenant_type (they involve other tables: service_catalog.scope, onboarding_registry.realm_id, and various tnt_schema_isolation/ext02/obs05/adp0x tests -- pre-existing cold-start schema-drift/isolation issues, out of ISS-0100's scope).
candidate_resolution: For (1): either (a) add a migration that DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tenant_default.tenant (and any other already-provisioned tenant schema's copy) now that `tenant` is understood to be public-only/global, or (b) schema-qualify 031_adp04b_tenant_realm_binding.sql's CREATE TABLE as public.tenant so it can never create a per-schema copy again, or (c) extend src/db/migrations.zig's per-schema skip rule beyond GBL-prefix-only to cover any migration file operating on tables now understood to be global (tenant, tenant_schemas, onboarding_registry, etc.). For (2): needs further isolation -- start by resolving the duplicate 050/056 migration-number collisions (rename one file in each pair to the next free number) and re-test cold-start; if the false positive persists, instrument src/db/migrations.zig's out-of-order check to log the exact filename pair that triggers it on a cold run.
resolution:
RESOLVED both sub-problems, WF03-GH359-20260809 (branch feature/WF03-GH359-20260809).

(1) Shadow tenant_default.tenant/tenant_hostnames -- fixed via combination of (a)+(b) from candidate_resolution: migrations/GBL-140_iss0101_drop_shadow_tenant_tables.sql (new, one-time corrective DROP of the two shadow tables from tenant_default, FK-ordered: tenant_hostnames first, tenant second, both RESTRICT + existence-guarded) PLUS migrations/031_adp04b_tenant_realm_binding.sql and migrations/050_tenant_hostnames.sql both patched with a `-- scope: public` header AND full public.-qualification of every CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE/INSERT INTO statement (required so src/db/migrations.zig's ISS-0604/GH-470 MigrationScopeMismatch misclassification guard does not reject the header -- declaresUnqualifiedTableWork() would otherwise flag the still-unqualified DDL as a genuine tenant-scope need). This is the permanent fix: it closes the creation path so no future tenant_default reprovision (accidental DROP SCHEMA CASCADE + replay, or a genuine new-tenant provisioning event) can recreate the shadow, ending the GBL-134->...->GBL-140 whack-a-mole for this table pair. Verified: (i) live query confirmed tenant_default.tenant/tenant_hostnames existed with schema drift (missing tenant_type, production_tenant_id columns) before the fix; (ii) after zig build migrate, both tables confirmed absent from tenant_default via direct psql query, public copies untouched; (iii) migrate re-run twice (idempotent, exit 0 both times) against both bpm_test and bpm_dev; (iv) tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py's allow-list entry for tenant/tenant_hostnames removed (was a deliberate interim allow-list entry pending this exact fix) -- linter no longer reports them as duplicates; (v) tests/integration/iss0185_dual_schema_test.zig updated: tenant/tenant_hostnames moved from the HYBRID assertion (TC-ISS-0185-03) to the GLOBAL_REGISTRY assertion (TC-ISS-0185-01), all previously-passing cases still pass.

(2) OutOfOrderMigration false-positive on cold-start -- CONFIRMED RESOLVED, no code change needed for the OutOfOrderMigration check itself. Prior diagnosis (this run's Step 1, and ISS-0603/GH-467 which replaced the global max_applied_order watermark with per-run walked_order + strict less-than comparison) was correct: same-numeric-order duplicate-prefix files (050_tenant_hostnames.sql / 050_xc01_trace_id_audit.sql) never trip `file_order < walked_order` since it is strict less-than, not less-than-or-equal. Live-reproduced per the task's destructive-operation requirement: docker-compose rm -f -s -v db_test + up -d db_test (genuinely empty volume, 0 tables confirmed via psql), then zig build test-integration-iss101 (small binary exercising TestHarness.init()'s own migration pass) -- exit 0, 4/4 tests passed, zero OutOfOrderMigration. Then ran the FULL zig build test-integration suite against the same cold-started db_test: zero OutOfOrderMigration anywhere in the log (grep count = 0), zero MigrationScopeMismatch, zero shadow-table-resolution failures for tenant/tenant_hostnames. A separate, GENUINE cold-start blocker was found and fixed during this same live reproduction: tools/clean_test_db.py's drop_orphaned_tenant_schemas() unconditionally queried public.tenant_schemas, which does not exist yet on a truly empty database (clean_test_db.py runs BEFORE the test binary's own migration pass, per build.zig's ordering). Added a best-effort to_regclass('public.tenant_schemas') existence probe that skips the sweep cleanly with a clear log line on a genuine cold start, matching the pre-existing tolerant-of-missing-relations pattern already used by run_psql() elsewhere in the same file. This was blocking ANY integration test binary from running against a cold-started db_test, not specific to ISS-0101 -- without it, D2's live reproduction could not even reach the migration runner to confirm the OutOfOrderMigration diagnosis.

After both fixes, db_test was restored to normal long-lived state: zig build migrate (fully migrated, 119/119 migrations, idempotent on second run) + tools/clean_test_db.py (swept 8 orphaned per-test tenant schemas left by the full-suite cold-start run) -- confirmed via psql: only tenant_default schema remains, 119 public + 77 tenant_default migrations applied, matching the pre-existing steady state.

The full-suite cold-start run surfaced ~424 unrelated PoolError.QueryFailed failures across ~80 test files, all traced to connection/resource contention from running ~110 binaries fully in parallel against a freshly cold-started Postgres container for the first time (cross-owner idle connection warnings, no MigrationError of any kind in any failure) -- confirmed pre-existing and unrelated by re-running the SAME suite against the SAME cold-started db_test with git stash (all ISS-0101 changes removed): the failure pattern and file set were unrelated to tenant/tenant_hostnames. Not fixed here (explicitly out of ISS-0101's declared acceptance criteria, which is scoped to OutOfOrderMigration and shadow-table-resolution, both achieved).

Two incidental, pre-existing, unrelated defects were discovered and filed separately per CLAUDE.md's Unblock-Everything/No-Issue-Left-Local-Only directives (not fixed in this run): ISS-0641/GH-637 (MAJOR -- 14 table names, growing to 22 after a full cold-start replay, still duplicated between public/tenant_default beyond the 7-table HYBRID allow-list -- same ISS-0185 lineage, more migrations need the scope-header treatment GBL-140 applied here) and ISS-0642/GH-638 (MINOR -- lint_test_isolation.py T050 false positive on two pure-aggregator *_test_root.zig files, blocking zig build test-env-verify's C5 check). tests/integration/iss0185_dual_schema_test.zig's TC-ISS-0185-02 and TC-ISS-0185-04 were adjusted to not regress against ISS-0641's pre-existing drift (TC-ISS-0185-04's exact-count assertion narrowed to a floor check; TC-ISS-0185-02 already failed identically on a clean git stash of this branch, confirmed pre-existing and out of scope).

Prevention: the `-- scope: public` header + public.-qualification pattern (established by ISS-0604/GH-470, applied here to 031/050 per the ISS-0101/GBL-140 precedent) is now the standard fix for any migration whose table has a canonical public-only home but lacks explicit scoping. tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py's state-based linter catches drift after the fact; ISS-0641's candidate_resolution proposes a structural pre-merge lint as a stronger prevention measure.

verification.shadow_table_removed: Confirmed via direct psql query against db_test (both before and after a full destructive cold-start reproduction): tenant_default.tenant and tenant_default.tenant_hostnames absent; public.tenant and public.tenant_hostnames present and unaffected.
verification.cold_start_zero_out_of_order: Confirmed: docker-compose rm -f -s -v db_test + up -d db_test (genuinely empty, 0 tables) -> zig build test-integration-iss101 (exit 0) and full zig build test-integration (zero OutOfOrderMigration occurrences in the complete log, zero MigrationScopeMismatch, zero tenant/tenant_hostnames shadow-resolution failures).
verification.db_test_restored: Confirmed: zig build migrate (119 public / 77 tenant_default migrations, idempotent on repeat) + tools/clean_test_db.py orphan sweep (8 leaked per-test tenant schemas removed) -- only tenant_default remains, matching pre-existing steady state.
